title: Remove legacy release bridge and split monolithic lint runner into staged fast/slow lanes
author: Maya Thompson
description:
Context: Our legacy 'release-bridge' action was a stopgap for signing and staging release artifacts during the early release automation rollout. It introduced hidden side effects (temporary S3 keys, long-lived ephemeral runners) and complicated our release path. At the same time, the monolithic lint job in .github/workflows/lint.yml bundles fast static checks with slow type-checking and formatting across all packages, which makes PR feedback slow and increases CI queue pressure.

This PR does two coordinated things in one change set: 1) Remove the legacy release-bridge code path and replace it with the consolidated, documented release-hooks workflow that uses the new release-agent composite action (already deployed to actions/rls-agent). 2) Split the monolithic lint runner into two staged lanes: "lint-fast" (pre-submit, lightweight JS/py linters, formatting, changed-file-based checks) and "lint-slow" (type-checks, full repo eslint --all, mypy full, style checks) that run in parallel when appropriate and on separate runner classes to reduce noise and improve median feedback time.

Why: Reduces CI tail latency, removes fragile artifact handling, simplifies release debugging, and gives teams control to opt into full checks for large refactors. Also reduces secrets exposure surface from ephemeral bridging code.

Checklist:
- [x] Remove .github/actions/release-bridge and ci/release_bridge.py
- [x] Add .github/workflows/release-hooks.yml using actions/rls-agent composite
- [x] Add .github/workflows/lint-fast.yml and .github/workflows/lint-slow.yml
- [x] Update README.ci and CONTRIBUTING.md with new lint expectations
- [x] Migrate a sample of active repos in monorepo config to opt-in for lint-slow on push
- [x] Add gating to ensure release-hooks validate signed-artefacts key rotation

Changes summary (high level):
- Removed: .github/actions/release-bridge/*, ci/release_bridge.py, scripts/bridging/README.md
- Added: .github/workflows/release-hooks.yml, .github/workflows/lint-fast.yml, .github/workflows/lint-slow.yml, .github/actions/rls-agent/ (reference only), ci/scripts/lint-split-helper.sh
- Modified: Makefile.ci (new targets: ci-lint-fast, ci-lint-slow), package.json (ci scripts), README.ci, CONTRIBUTING.md, docs/release/automation.md

Commits (summary):
- refactor(ci): introduce lint-fast/lint-slow workflow templates
- feat(actions): wire release-hooks to actions/rls-agent composite action
- chore(ci): remove legacy release-bridge action and support scripts
- docs: update CI docs and troubleshooting steps for new flows

Testing & verification:
- Local: ran lint-fast against changed-file set and lint-slow on a sampled feature branch (no regressions).
- CI: lint-fast matrix run (node versions: 18, 20) passed; lint-slow required a single rerun due to a transient mypy network dependency which we addressed by pinning an internal stub. Release-hooks ran in a dry-run against staging artifacts and validated signature flow.

Rollout plan:
- Merge to main behind a short freeze window (we coordinated with SRE).
- Roll-forward: opt-in per-package for lint-slow over next 2 weeks using monorepo config.
- Fall-back: ability to reintroduce release-bridge via a short-lived branch if an edge-case fails.

Related: ENG-1122 (CI feedback latency), ENG-1199 (release automation hardening).
